It guarantees that the disease will be cured within a year.

questions.question: Which of the following criteria is LEAST relevant when determining the strength of an analogical argument?

The number of relevant similarities versus relevant dissimilarities.
The personal popularity of the person who originally invented the analogy.
The presence of critical differences that break the core mechanism of comparison.

Translating the original argument into another language.
Proving that the opponent lacks a formal degree in logic.
Offering a different analogy that leads to an opposite conclusion, highlighting more fitting similarities to the current case.

questions.question: In evaluating a scientific claim that compares the human brain to a modern digital computer, what is a fundamental disanalogy pointed out by critics?

Brains require electricity, while computers run entirely without power sources.

questions.question: Why might an analogy used to support a controversial government intervention fail under close logical scrutiny?

The underlying mechanisms of the intervention and the historical example share superficial traits but differ fundamentally in legal and operational constraints.
The analogy was printed in black and white instead of color.

Oil is generated entirely by digital algorithms.

They present instances where the analogy's suggested cause-and-effect relationship fails to hold true.

Whether cultural transmission involves Lamarckian inheritance (acquired traits passed down), which fundamentally differs from genetic natural selection.
If the cultural trends are popular on social media.

Editorial: 'Since the introduction of the new wellness program at our company, employees have taken fewer sick days. Thus, the wellness program is solely responsible for improving the overall health of our staff.' What is the logical flaw?

options.option: It ignores the cost of implementing the wellness program.
It overlooks other potential explanations for the decrease in sick days, such as seasonal variations or fewer flu outbreaks.
It assumes that taking sick days is always a fraudulent practice.
It presumes that employees who take fewer sick days are more productive.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Most successful entrepreneurs read at least one business book a week. Therefore, if you start reading a business book every week, you will inevitably become a successful entrepreneur.' Which of the following best describes the flaw?

options.option: It confuses a correlation or necessary condition with a sufficient condition.
It generalizes from a sample size that is too small to be meaningful.
It attacks the character of entrepreneurs rather than their arguments.
It uses circular reasoning to prove its primary claim.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Critics argue that our new tax policy will hurt the economy, but these critics are mostly disgruntled politicians who just want to win the upcoming election. Therefore, the tax policy is completely sound.' What is the flaw?

options.option: It assumes that all politicians are dishonest.
It relies on emotional appeal rather than logical analysis of the economy.
It misinterprets statistical data regarding past tax policies.
It commits an ad hominem fallacy by attacking the critics' motives rather than addressing the policy itself.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Since no one has ever been able to prove conclusively that extraterrestrial life does not exist, it is certain that aliens have visited Earth.' Which of the following best identifies the flaw?

options.option: It assumes that space is infinite in scale.
It uses ambiguous terminology regarding what constitutes 'extraterrestrial life'.
It appeals to ignorance by treating a lack of evidence for a claim as evidence for its opposite.
It draws a sweeping conclusion based on a single eyewitness account.

questions.question: Editorial: 'The hospital implemented a new hygiene protocol, and subsequently, infection rates dropped by 20%. Therefore, the new protocol is the sole reason for the improvement.' What flaw is present?

options.option: It relies on data collected over an insufficient time period.
It assumes a causal relationship merely based on chronological sequence (post hoc ergo propter hoc).
It ignores the opinions of the medical staff regarding the protocol.
It generalizes from a single hospital to all medical facilities nationwide.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Everyone in our neighborhood loves the new park. Thus, every single resident in the entire city will support building more parks.' What is the primary logical flaw?

options.option: It assumes that parks are inexpensive to construct and maintain.
It uses circular logic to prove the economic benefits of parks.
It confuses public property with private real estate ownership.
It commits a fallacy of hasty generalization by applying a local, non-representative sample to an entire population.

questions.question: Editorial: 'If we ban the sale of sugary drinks, people will become healthier. If people become healthier, they will live longer. Therefore, banning sugary drinks will completely eliminate human mortality.' Which flaw is evident?

options.option: It relies on unverified medical statistics from an unknown source.
It assumes that sugary drinks are the only cause of poor health.
It extends a reasonable premise to an absurd or extreme conclusion through slippery slope exaggeration.
It attacks the beverage industry rather than evaluating health metrics.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Our company should adopt this new software because both Competitor X and Competitor Y are using it to manage their projects.' What is the logical flaw?

options.option: It fails to account for employee training costs.
It implies that the software is completely free of bugs.
It assumes that what works or is appropriate for competitors is automatically right for our company (bandwagon/imitation fallacy).
It relies on outdated market research.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Either we completely abolish all environmental regulations, or our manufacturing sector will be entirely destroyed.' Which flaw does this argument commit?

options.option: It assumes that environmental regulations cost nothing to enforce.
It uses circular reasoning to justify the abolition of laws.
It presents a false dilemma by artificially limiting choices to two extreme options while ignoring moderate alternatives.
It relies on testimony from biased industrial lobbyists.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Professor Smith's theory on macroeconomic trends cannot be trusted because he recently received a parking ticket.' What is the exact flaw in this reasoning?

options.option: It commits an ad hominem fallacy by attacking an irrelevant personal failing of the speaker rather than evaluating their professional argument.
It uses circular logic to discredit academic credentials.
It misrepresents macroeconomic data to make a petty point.
It assumes that parking tickets are distributed unfairly.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Since the ancient philosophers studied the stars and believed in astrology, modern astrophysics must also be based on superstition.' What flaw is present here?

options.option: It relies on circular logic to dismiss empirical physics.
It attacks astronomers instead of evaluating their telescopes.
It commits a genetic fallacy by judging a modern concept solely based on its historical origins or associations.
It assumes that ancient philosophers were infallible.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Heavy consumption of red meat has been linked to various health issues. Therefore, eating a single hamburger once a year will instantly cause fatal health problems.' What flaw does this commit?

options.option: It uses circular reasoning regarding dietary preferences.
It assumes that hamburgers are made entirely of vegetables.
It relies on data from agricultural lobbies.
It commits a fallacy of accident or sweeping generalization by ignoring the difference between moderate and heavy consumption.

options.option: It uses circular logic to define corporate profit.
It assumes that mergers never fail under any circumstances.
It attacks shareholders rather than evaluating financial reports.
It relies on an appeal to misplaced authority or prestige, assuming success in one area guarantees prediction accuracy in another.

It relies on testimony from biased corporate executives.
It confuses the absence of evidence proving guilt with positive evidence of innocence.
It attacks the judicial system rather than examining the financial records.

It assumes that all students play video games every single day.

questions.question: Editorial: 'Since the new traffic signal was installed at Main Street, accidents have decreased by 50%. Therefore, traffic signals are the only possible solution to urban safety issues.' What is the flaw?

It ignores the color of the traffic light.
It assumes that traffic signals cost nothing to install.
It relies on self-reported driver surveys.

questions.question: Editorial: 'We know that meditation reduces stress because people who meditate report feeling much calmer.' What logical flaw is present?

It assumes that subjective self-reporting is definitive proof without objective physiological measurements.
It relies on anonymous sources from online forums.
It ignores the financial cost of meditation classes.

It relies on outdated civil engineering models.
